prompt: Five equally spaced equilibrium positions 0,12,24,36,48 mm have ξ=+2,0,−2,0,+2 mm. Draw displacement and actual spacing, then plot qualitative pressure signs on intervals.

Five equilibrium particles spaced 10 mm apart have measured gaps 11,9,8,12 mm. A report gives displacement [0,1,0,−2,0] mm as the only solution. Construct a different compatible profile, identify the missing constraint, and recover the profile if the fourth particle is known at displacement +1 mm.
Three equilibrium positions 0,15,30 mm have displacements −2,+1,+1 mm. A report says the negatively displaced particle marks rarefaction. Explain what the data actually establish about each gap.

Two pulses arrive at 2 and 6 ms. An intervention lengthens a known solid segment by 4 m at 2000 m/s, but leaves air geometry unchanged. New arrivals are 4 and 6 ms. Assess competing path labels and propose a further test.

Two paths connect a transmitter and sensor. Route X crosses 0.9 m at 300 m/s and 3 m at 1500 m/s. Route Y is a 4 m solid path at 2000 m/s. Construct a labelled time diagram with segment transitions and arrival order.

A tap on a pipe is detected early by a contact sensor and later by a microphone. Covering the microphone's air inlet reduces the later signal, while the pipe sensor is unchanged. Explain the possible paths and why timing alone is not enough to identify them.

The third and tenth peaks of a fixed microphone signal occur at 5 and 19 ms. At one instant the second and eighth matching compressions are at 0.40 and 4.36 m. Infer T, f, λ and v; decide whether 320–340 m/s is consistent.

Successive upward zero crossings on a time trace are at 0.5 and 2.5 ms. A spatial snapshot has successive downward zero crossings at 0.30 and 0.98 m. Draw a complete sinusoidal cycle for each with extrema and crossing slopes labelled; determine T, f, λ and v.

A sinusoidal trace shows consecutive zero crossings separated by 0.8 ms. Two spatial compressions separated by 0.544 m are visible but the intervening region is missing. A report gives f=1250 Hz and λ=0.544 m. Challenge or defend the report, and specify what observation makes speed unique.

A pulse arrives after 5.5 ms at 1.05 m and 9.5 ms at 2.45 m using one apparatus. A third distance of 3.50 m gives 12.5 ms. Find speed and offset and decide whether the readings support the fixed-delay model.

A steady source of 400 Hz sends sound across a 0.9 m section with λ=0.75 m followed by 0.6 m with λ=1.25 m. Sketch cumulative travel time versus path distance at all three boundaries and infer overall speed.

A 2 m direct path contains unknown length x in medium A and the rest in B. A 500 Hz source has λA=0.60 m and λB=1.00 m. The apparatus reports 7.2 ms through the mixed path and 5.6 ms through 2 m entirely in B. Both have the same unknown delay. A separate 1 m path entirely in A reports 4.933 ms (rounded). Find x and delay, and assess consistency.

At 2 m and 4 m from a source, a calibrated pressure sensor reports peak amplitudes 8 and 4 Pa. At 8 m it reports 1 Pa. Test ideal isotropic lossless spreading in one medium and infer what the data do and do not establish.

Trace A repeats an upward zero crossing every 4 ms and has peak-to-peak pressure 6 Pa. Trace B has successive pressure maxima 2 ms apart and peak-to-peak 3 Pa. Draw one full cycle of each on common scales; compare pitch and intensity in the same medium.

A displacement trace for tone A has twice the displacement amplitude of tone B but half its frequency. Both are progressive linear waves. The medium for each is not specified. A report claims IA>IB and A must sound louder. Decide whether the evidence proves either claim; use I∝ρv(fA_displacement)² and construct two compatible impedance cases with opposite intensity order.

A left-moving periodic sinusoidal displacement pattern with λ=0.40 m, amplitude 2 mm and initial trough x=0.10 m has speed 300 m/s. Construct two profiles on 0≤x≤0.80 m separated by 1 ms; identify the later value at x=0.10 m.

A sinusoidal displacement wave with λ=0.90 m produces the same spatial profile at times separated by 5 ms. A report concludes the material has travelled at 180 m/s. A separate instrument bounds propagation speed to 150–400 m/s. Reject or defend the report and identify every compatible signed propagation velocity.

A periodic pressure wave has λ=1.00 m. At 5 ms a second snapshot has its maxima displaced +0.25 m modulo λ. The speed lies from 100 to 450 m/s inclusive, direction unknown. At 2 ms the maxima have moved +0.30 m modulo λ. Recover signed velocity and justify uniqueness.
Two sensors (one emits) are 6 m apart parallel to a wall at equal unknown distance. Echo delay after direct sound is 10 ms, v=400 m/s. Recover the wall distance and test a proposed 2 m result.
Source 2 m and receiver 10 m from a wall have parallel separation 6 m. v=340 m/s. Calculate both path times and assess a 12 ms separation requirement.

A receiver records direct arrival at 24 ms and reflected at 40 ms after a pulse. v=250 m/s, equal normal wall distances. Draw the time trace and corresponding image-source geometry, infer normal distance.

An untreated hall and a treated hall both show direct arrival at0 and late group at40 ms, but the treated late amplitude is smaller. A student concludes the panels did not reduce reverberation because the timing is the same. Give a counterexample and a more relevant measurement.

A hall's late sound becomes weaker after adding absorptive panels, while measured arrival times of two still-detectable returns remain unchanged. Explain the observations and why unchanged timing does not mean the treatment failed.

Model X has returns at 12 and 48 ms, amplitudes0.8,0.5. Model Y adds a 28 ms return at amplitude0.25. Direct amplitude1. Detector threshold0.4, duration18 ms, required quiet gap6 ms; observed groups 0–30 and48–66 ms. Threshold then drops to0.2 at duration18 ms, yielding one group 0–66 ms. Finally duration drops to4 ms at threshold0.2. Determine which model fits and predict final separate starts, and explain whether the second trace alone proves there are exactly three reflection paths.

Known normal reflectors at 6 and18 m return at 11 and27 ms. At 30 m an independent return is44 ms. Fit common speed/delay and assess the exact third observation; give conditional range for a 35 ms return if the first model were used.

A pulse-echo detector reports a reference at 4 m in uniform medium speed1000 m/s after 10 ms. A normal target beyond a 5 m first layer at1000 m/s and a second medium at1500 m/s returns after 24 ms. Same fixed delay. Find target distance.

Two pulse-echo units A=(0,0), B=(8,0) m share known speed1500 m/s and common unknown delay. A known 3 m reflector returns at6 ms. The same stationary unknown target returns at 10 ms from both A and B. A third calibrated unit C=(0,6) records a return at approximately7.508 ms with same delay. Determine the target candidates from A/B, then use C to select and verify the location.

A fixed-end string gives120 Hz. Length becomes 3/4 of original, tension becomes9/4 original and μ fixed. Measured f is240 Hz. Test the ideal model and the length-only explanation; give a further prediction if tension returns to original.

Two instruments produce spectra with only one detected peak at400 Hz under a narrow-band sensor. A technician concludes they must share the same fundamental and instrument type. Construct two compatible source explanations and specify an improved measurement.

A wind instrument plays a higher note when a hole is opened. Its microphone amplitude decreases. Explain how effective vibrating air-column length and radiation/detection can lead to different pitch and amplitude trends.
